text:
Dubai registered 13,707 residential sales valued at AED 39,487,272,167 in the last four weeks, a 24.1 percent increase in volume and 23.1 percent in value compared to the previous four weeks. A separate 5,556 mortgage registrations were recorded during the same period. The market remains heavily weighted toward off-plan transactions, which accounted for 56.7 percent of all sales.

The median residential price per square foot rose to AED 1,727, representing a 3.4 percent increase from the prior four-week median of AED 1,671. Top performing areas by volume include Dubai South with 2,736 sales and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,521 sales over the last twelve weeks. Dubai Creek Harbour commands the highest median price at AED 2,528 per square foot among the top eight communities.

Rental activity shows 107,552 contracts registered with a 51.9 percent renewal share. The median residential rent stands at AED 68,000 per year. Estimated gross yields vary significantly by location, with International City Phase 1 leading at 8.6 percent for flats, followed by Zaabeel First at 8.0 percent. Town Square, Dubai Sports City, and Dubai Production City follow with yields of 6.9, 6.6, and 6.4 percent respectively.

Price momentum is mixed across the city. Al Yufrah 1 shows the strongest heating with a 33.8 percent twelve-week price increase, while Saih Shuaib 1 is cooling with a 29.6 percent decline. An anomaly monitor flagged 980 sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35 percent away from their comparable median. These figures are based on registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial shares, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
